promise.role: Diagnose and correct effective Unit of Work, Identity Map and Lazy Load behavior.
promise.activation: Unexpected/missing persistence, query growth, stale managed state after bulk work, slow/growing persistence context, lazy initialization failure or OSIV used to hide a loading issue.
promise.outOfScope: Mapping design, data-access pattern selection, transaction architecture and cache design remain referred to the existing neighboring skills.
promise.evidenceRequired: Resolved runtime/mapping/flush mode, owning context and transaction, loaded-state history, SQL/parameters/query counts and fresh-context state after transaction completion.
promise.deliverable: Observed symptom, conditional mechanism, confirming/refuting evidence and smallest adequate fix or justified no-change.

reviewCriteria: Persistence identity is scoped to the effective context, not a query cache or cross-context identity guarantee.
Dirty checking, flush, commit, rollback, bulk SQL and merge must remain distinct.
Loading recommendations follow actual initialized state, mapping, access and context/thread ownership.
Simple adequate fetching, intentional merge/editing and deliberate OSIV remain viable.
Performance conclusions require actual query/workload evidence; no universal batching or fetching claim.
Failure recovery respects lifecycle ownership and stale-version/partial-input requirements.

correctedFindings.finding: The Jakarta Persistence 3.2 URL omitted the .html suffix and returned HTTP 404.
correctedFindings.consequence: The source link could not support direct verification of consequential persistence contracts.
correctedFindings.evidence: GET old URL=404; GET corrected URL=200 with Jakarta Persistence title. All eight final primary resource URLs in the package returned 200.

changedFiles.change: One source URL corrected; no semantic wording changed.

preserved: All activation conditions, description, package dependencies, suggests and read-source capability.
Context-scoped identity versus query caching and separate persistence contexts.
Writable dirty checking without save, query-triggered flush, commit/rollback distinctions and fresh-context verification.
Merge return ownership, provider-unfetched state versus reconstructed defaults, caller expected-version protection.
Failed-flush disposal through lifecycle owner; clear is not transaction recovery; expected no-result remains distinct.
Flush-order and JDBC batching qualifications, context/transaction cost distinctions, target-version stateless semantics.
N+1, conditional EAGER/fetch graph/batch/subselect choices, collection-pagination and topology distinctions.
Loaded-state/session/thread boundaries; deliberate adequate OSIV, entity representation and detached-edit alternatives.
Bulk operation staleness/versioning, selective reconciliation, equality/hash caution and aggregate-statistics limitations.

Added explicit expected-version comparison to the editor adapter to keep the adequate case free of an unrelated stale-edit ambiguity; recompiled the changed pair and ran both profiles plus a stale-input control. Earlier and final logs are retained; final pair logs are authoritative.

data.sharedTask: Revise o job de alteração de email. A operação autorizada pode alterar apenas o email de um contato existente; telefones devem continuar intactos. Preserve o controle de versão do editor e o comportamento já adequado. Investigue o caminho efetivo de entrada, a gravação e a leitura após commit, usando os artefatos. Recomende a menor correção necessária, ou justifique manter o código quando suficiente. Não atualize dependências.

data.decisiveConstraint: The object passed to merge originates either from a real Hibernate-loaded detached instance with an unfetched persistent collection, or from a freshly reconstructed entity whose empty collection is ordinary state.
common: Trace EmailUpdateJob.input and execute; verify contacts/phones mapping and version.
Check fresh-context email and phone rows after commit; SQL emission or in-memory values alone are insufficient.
Do not confuse merge's managed result with reattachment, or assume every null/default/unloaded field is ignored.
Preserve expected-version conflict behavior and avoid blanket bans on merge, eager fetching or DTO mandates.

criteria: Unfetched provider-tracked phones are ignored by merge; original rows survive.
The shown deliberately edited detached graph is adequate for this operation when its editor owns state/version; no forced rewrite solely because merge appears.
Observable: updated email, one stored phone for contact 7.
Reconstruction supplies a plain empty collection, not provider-tracked unloaded state; cascade/orphan removal can delete the existing phone.
Recommend applying explicitly allowed email changes to a managed instance with the caller's expected-version check, or an equivalent contract-preserving patch operation.
Observable original job: updated email but zero phones for contact 7. A fix must retain phone and reject stale expected versions.

negativeControls: Do not treat a current version as proof that omission means preservation.
Simply use the result of merge, add save or refresh after commit does not undo orphan deletion.
Loading latest state without preserving the stale-edit precondition loses conflict protection.
